issues.title: The Typewriter With a Magic Eye
issues.teaser: A best-selling Chinese novelist spent his fortune on a typewriter that never went on sale, and quietly changed what it means to type.

issues.title: The Necklaces Nobody Could Keep
issues.teaser: Stranded in the Pacific by war, a young anthropologist found islanders trading shell valuables they could barely wear and were not allowed to keep.

issues.title: The Tea Master in the Snow
issues.teaser: A Japanese lord with no prospects spent his youth on tea. His phrase for treating every gathering as the only one outlived him.

issues.title: The Dirty First Pages
issues.teaser: An astronomer noticed that the first pages of logarithm books wore out fastest. The reason turned into a law that now helps catch fraudsters.

issues.title: The Stars on the Shrine Wall
issues.teaser: A physics student in Uzbekistan noticed ten-pointed stars on a madrasa wall. They led him to five tiles and a pattern far ahead of its time.

issues.title: The Jesuit Who Remembered Backwards
issues.teaser: In 1595 an Italian Jesuit in Ming China astonished scholars by repeating lists of characters backwards. His secret was an ancient trick of places.

issues.title: Twenty-Seven Dollars in Jobra
issues.teaser: A Bangladeshi economics professor found 42 villagers trapped by $27 of debt, and a bank that said the poor were not creditworthy.

issues.title: The Man Who Sang an Odyssey
issues.teaser: In 1935 a Bosnian singer who could not read dictated an epic as long as the Odyssey to an American scholar hunting for Homer.

issues.title: The Cockatoos Across the Strait
issues.teaser: In 1856 a young naturalist sailed from Bali to Lombok, a short hop, and found himself among the birds of a different continent.

issues.title: The Waiter Who Forgot the Bill
issues.teaser: A Berlin waiter reportedly forgot a table’s order once the bill was settled. A Lithuanian student turned the puzzle into a famous effect.

issues.title: Seven Days Staring at Bamboo
issues.concept: The unity of knowledge and action
issues.teaser: A young Chinese scholar tried to find the truth in a bamboo grove, fell ill, and years later found it somewhere else.

issues.title: The Emperor Who Said Sorry
issues.teaser: Around 260 BC an Indian emperor won a brutal war, then had his regret carved into rock across his empire.

issues.title: The Man Who Doubted the Sea
issues.teaser: On a voyage home from England in 1921, an Indian physicist refused to believe the sea was just reflecting the sky.

issues.title: The Art of Not Trying
issues.teaser: A Renaissance parlour game at the court of Urbino gave the world its rule for elegance: never let them see you try.

issues.title: The Speckled Axe
issues.teaser: Benjamin Franklin tried to make himself morally perfect with a notebook and some red ink. He failed, and was glad he tried.

issues.title: The Ending Hemingway Left Out
issues.teaser: Why Hemingway cut the most dramatic thing in a story, and why it made the story stronger.

issues.title: The Horse Who Could Count
issues.teaser: A Berlin horse who did arithmetic, a panel of experts who were fooled, and the psychologist who worked out what was really going on.

issues.title: The Great Hanoi Rat Hunt
issues.teaser: How a bounty on rat tails left colonial Hanoi with more rats, not fewer.
